paragraphs.source_en: 172 THE OTTOMANS Benefiting from Spain’s expulsion of its Muslims, the Ottomans utilised the Moriscos—Muslims converted to Catholicism who remained in Spain—as spies and agents. They encouraged uprisings in Spain by supplying firearms and ammunition, coordinating the Morisco attacks with their own naval campaigns in North Africa.’ The Ottomans facilitated contacts between Moriscos and Moroccans and encouraged them to unite with Protestants in the Habsburg Netherlands against their oppressive overlords.

paragraphs.source_en: Recognising that the Ottomans tolerated religious minorities whereas their own emperor did not, anti-Habsburg rebels in the Netherlands promoted the slogan ‘Rather Turkish than Popish’, even minting the motto on crescent-bedecked coins in the 1570s.** Whether actualised or not, the threat of Ottoman support of Morisco and Protestant rebellion in that era—Selim II and the Dutch prince William I of Orange sent secret envoys to each other’s courts to discuss such plans—diverted Habsburg forces and helped the Ottomans accomplish their military aims.*°
